notes: The handwritten sheet number is 28. The page names the constructed Inf for the refinement relation the “figure intersection” F.G. It distinguishes that construction from the set intersection F∩G in general, says they coincide for compatible figures, and asserts an arbitrary-family version with support equal to the intersection of supports. These assertions are transcribed, not independently proved here.

The underlined word after “propriété de” is modération: the initial m, o, looped d, accented following letter and terminal -tion are visible. H’s demi-treillis is not supported by those letters. The preceding l’apparente is preferred with s’apparente retained, and the cancelled phrase remains doubtful. No mathematical expectation was used to settle either.

The cancelled footer states that F′≼F entails F′.G≼F.G and adds “(Immédiat sur supports) : Subdivision induite sur un raffinement.” Its assertion of immediacy is the author’s, not a completed check in this run. The entire footer and its smaller nested cancellation are preserved. H already describes the broad cancellation in an editorial note, so conversion of that description into the edition’s deleted macro is excluded from substantive counts.

The compatibility sentence visibly omits sont; none is supplied. The insertion en général has a curved guide above the live la figure, not a strike through those words. The first footer relation has retracing but no separately recoverable cancelled sign. No title, date, explicit question or verbal reservation occurs on this sheet.

The blind audit prefers l’apparente, with s’apparente retained, from the tall initial stem. This potentially awkward syntax is not repaired. The crossed word after F cap G now prefers quand, with the earlier inter./intersection alternatives retained. A low mark within the first P(L) is preserved as a doubtful comma-like mark/subscript1, with absence also possible. The conjectural old y/l before live l’appelle is omitted: its disconnected brown patches and pale ragged halo favour a surface artefact. Rubbed old ink remains a physical alternative in the doubts record; no definite authorial cancellation is asserted there.
